issues.description: Method addGuestStudents: The problem statement's textual task (problem_statement.md) requests addGuestStudents(String) (a String parameter), while the UML in the same problem statement and the solution implementation both declare addGuestStudents(int) (an int parameter). This inconsistency (String vs int) makes it unclear which parameter type students should implement and may lead to implementations that don't match the tests or the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter type consistent across all artifacts. Recommended: change the textual instruction in problem_statement.md (line 50) to request addGuestStudents(int) to match the UML and the solution, and add a short clarifying sentence and example that the parameter is the number of new guest students (an integer). If instead the intent was to accept a String, update the UML, template TODO, and solution implementation to use String and update any tests accordingly.

issues.description: The concept is adding new guest students to a Lecture. In problem_statement.md (textual task description) the method is written as addGuestStudents(String). In the same problem statement UML the method is declared as addGuestStudents(int). The template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) contains a TODO for addGuestStudents but no signature, and the solution implementation defines public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). This mismatch between the textual description (String) and the UML/solution (int) creates ambiguity for students about the expected parameter type and may cause implementations that don't match the tests or reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter type consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: update problem_statement.md (line 50) to require addGuestStudents(int) so it matches the UML (line 73), the template TODO, and the solution implementation. If a String parameter is intentionally required, update the template and solution to declare addGuestStudents(String) and document/implement parsing and error handling, and update tests accordingly.
